Subaida vs The Secretary on 9 February, 2024 
Author: N.Nagaresh
Bench: N.Nagaresh
 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam
 Present
 The Honourable Mr.Justice N.Nagaresh
 Friday, The 9Th Day Of February 2024 / 20Th Magha, 1945
 Wp(C) No. 1130 Of 2024
Petitioner:
 Subaida
 Aged 50 Years
 W/O Hamza, Valiyakualthingal,
 Deshabimani Road, Dewaswomparambu,
 Elamakkara P.O, Ernakulam, Pin - 682026
 By Adv V.V.Suresh 
Respondent:
 The Secretary
 Kochi Municipal Corporation,
 Kochi Municipal Corporation Office,
 Park Avenue Road, Marine Drive Kochi,
 Ernakulam, Pin - 682011
 By Adv K. Janardhana Shenoy 
 This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For
Admission On 09.02.2024, The Court On The Same Day
Delivered The Following:
 Wp(C) No.1130 of 2024
 2
 Judgment 
Dated this the 9th day of February, 2024 The petitioner is aggrieved by the action on the part of the respondent-Secretary to Kochi Municipal Corporation taking steps to evict the petitioner and forcefully taking over her authorized bunk from the roadside, without proper notice or intimation.
2. The petitioner is a lady, who conducts business of cool drinks in a bunk near Pottakuzhy Church on the side of Pottakuzhy- Pachalam road. On 08.01.2024, the officials and cleaning staff of the Subaida vs The Secretary on 9 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175932046/
1 Kochi Corporation entered her bunk and they tried to take all the items and the bunk, in a lorry and ordered her not to continue her business there. But, they were interrupted by all the other persons who conducted roadside business there. The petitioner requested the Corporation officials not to remove the bunk from there where she has been conducting business for the past eight years, stating that she has a valid licence from the Kochi Corporation for conducting business there. So, they have not taken her belongings. But they wanted her to close the bunk and business. 
3. On further enquiry with the Corporation Office, it is informed that the Corporation had insisted all the street vendors to submit an affidavit during the month of December, 2022 and most of them submitted that affidavit. But at that time, due to rheumatic problems the petitioner closed her bunk for two months for her treatment. Therefore, the petitioner was unable to submit that affidavit before the Kochi Corporation. Nobody informed her regarding this. Thereafter, the petitioner had not received any notice or any intimation from the Kochi Corporation regarding this matter. 
4. The petitioner filed a detailed representation before the respondent regarding this matter. The petitioner is ready and willing to submit any documents or affidavit with fine to condone the delay,
if any. Without any notice the Corporation Authorities are trying to stop her business. Hence, the petitioner is before this Court. 
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondent. 
6. The grievance of the petitioner is relating to a decision of the Town Vending Committee. Section 11 of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 provides that any person who is aggrieved by any decision of the Town Vending Committee with respect to issue of Certificate of Vending under Section 6 or cancellation or suspension of Certificate of Vending under Section 10 may prefer an appeal to the local authority in such form, within such period, and in such manner, as may be prescribed. As the petitioner has an effective alternate remedy under the Act, 2014, I am of the view that the petitioner shall resort to the appellate remedy first before approaching this Court with the writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. 
The writ petition is therefore disposed of directing that the petitioner may file an Appeal before the Town Vending Committee under Section 11 of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014. If the petitioner submits an Appeal within two weeks, the same shall be considered on merits and orders passed within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of the Appeal. 
Sd/-
